questions.question: Which government body regulates food safety in India?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) is the main government body
  • responsible for regulating food safety in India. FSSAI sets standards for food products and
  • oversees their manufacture, storage, distribution, sale, and import to ensure safe and
  • wholesome food for consumers.

questions.question: What is food borne illness?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: Food borne illness are the diseases caused by agents entering human body through the
  • ingestion of food. Most common symptoms are gastro-intestinal in nature. It is usually
  • caused by bacteria, viruses, parasites, or chemical substances.
questions.final_answer: caused by bacteria, viruses, parasites, or chemical substances

questions.question: Why is food safety important for public health?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: Food safety is important for public health because it helps prevent food-borne illnesses
  • that can cause serious health problems or even death.
  • • Prevention of food borne illness.
  • • Protection of vulnerable individuals.
  • • Boosting of consumer confidence.
  • • Protection of producer.
  • • Improved Productivity.

questions.question: What is the difference between cleaning and sanitization?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: Cleaning- It is the process of removing visible dirt, dust, food residues from the
  • surfaces.
  • Sanitization- It reduces the number of germs on surfaces to a safe level, involves using
  • chemicals or heat after cleaning.

questions.question: What is the risk associated with food hazards?

questions.question: What is a chemical food hazard? Provide an example.
questions.solution_html:

questions.question: What is water activity (aw) ?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: Water activity is how much free water is available in a food product for microbial
  • growth, chemical reactions and enzymatic activity. It is the ratio of the vapour pressure of
  • water present in food substrate to the vapour pressure of pure water at the same
  • temperature.

questions.question: Define microorganisms

  • and additionally due to contamination during harvesting, processing, storage and
  • distribution. They include a wide variety of life forms such as, Bacteria, Viruses, Fungi and
  • Protozoa.

questions.question: How moisture content affects the growth of microorganisms?

questions.question: What are the key factors that determine the quality of food? Explain any / five.
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: The quality of food is determined by various factors that ensure it is safe, nutritious
  • and acceptable to consumers. Here are five key factors
  • • Nutritional Value- Presence of essential nutrients such as carbohydrates, proteins
  • fats, vitamins, and minerals in the right proportions.
  • • Freshness- Fresh food is free from spoilage and degradation. It has a natural flavor
  • aroma, and texture.
  • • Hygiene and Safety- Food should be free from harmful bacteria, viruses, chemicals
  • and physical contaminants.
  • • Taste and Appearance- Sensory qualities such as color, flavor, texture, and aroma play
  • a major role in consumer acceptance.
questions.final_answer: a major role in consumer acceptance

questions.question: Discuss the health hazards caused by chemical contaminants in food?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: Chemical contaminants in food are harmful substances that can enter the food supply
  • during farming, processing, packaging, or storage. These contaminants pose serious health
  • hazards.
  • • Acute Poisoning- High levels of chemicals such as pesticides or cleaning agents can
  • cause immediate symptoms like nausea, vomiting, dizziness, abdominal pain, and
  • even death in extreme cases.
  • • Chronic effect- long term exposure to low level of chemicals can lead to serious
  • health problems like cancer, kidney damage and neurological disorders.
  • • Organ damage- Exposure to certain chemicals can damage specific organs like liver or
  • kidney.
  • • Developmental effects- In children, exposure to chemicals can impacts mental
  • intellectual and physical level.
  • • Reproductive issues- Chemical exposure may lead to reproductive problems and birth
  • defects.

questions.question: How food infection can be defined?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: Food infection refers to a type of foodborne illness that occurs when a person
  • consumes food or water contaminated with pathogenic microorganisms, such as bacteria
  • viruses, or parasites.
  • • Cause- The ingestion of live microorganisms such as Salmonella, E. coli.
  • • Mechanism- After consumption, the pathogens colonize the gastrointestinal tract
  • and start reproducing, leading to the release of toxins or causing direct damage to
  • the tissues.
  • • Symptoms- Fever, diarrhoea, abdominal cramps, nausea, and vomiting.
  • • Sources- Contaminated water, undercooked meat, unpasteurized milk, raw
  • vegetables, and unhygienically prepared food.
  • • Prevention- Proper cooking, personal hygiene, safe food handling, and clean water
  • supply.

questions.question: Explain morphological characteristics of bacteria?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: Bacteria are microscopic, single-celled organisms that vary in shape, size, and
  • arrangement.
  • • Shape- Cocci (Spherical), Bacilli (Rod), Spirilla (Spiral or helical), Vibrios
  • • Size- Range from 0.2 to 2.0 micrometers in diameter and 1 to 10 micrometers in
  • length. Cocci are generally smaller than bacilli.
  • • Flagella and Motility- Bacteria have flagella, which are tail-like structures used for
  • movement.
  • • Cell Wall Structure.

questions.question: Describe incidental adulteration and its sources in food processing.
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: Incidental adulteration refers to the unintentional contamination of food products that
  • occurs during various stages of food production, processing, packaging, transportation, or
  • storage.
  • • Contaminated Equipment and Machinery- Adulterated due to rust, grease, or metal
  • particles from poorly maintained machines or processing equipment.
  • • Improper Storage Conditions- Food stored in damp, unhygienic, or infested
  • warehouses.
  • • Use of Contaminated Water- Using unclean or chemically contaminated water during
  • washing, processing, or mixing.
  • • Pesticide and Chemical Residues- Excessive or improper use of pesticides during
  • farming can leave chemical residues.
  • • Packaging Materials- Food may get contaminated through chemicals from low-grade
  • plastic or recycled packaging materials, which can leach into the food during storage.
questions.final_answer: plastic or recycled packaging materials, which can leach into the food during storage

questions.question: Explain how food adulteration affects the economy and public health.
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: Food adulteration has serious consequences for both public health and the economy. It
  • involves the addition of inferior or harmful substances to food, which can lead to
  • widespread harm and loss.
  • • Health Hazards and Diseases- cause a range of health issues such as food poisoning
  • cancer, liver and kidney damage, neurological disorders, and in severe cases, death.
  • • Malnutrition- Reduce the nutritional quality of food, leading to deficiencies and
  • weakened immunity, especially in vulnerable groups like children and the elderly.
  • • Long-Term Chronic Illnesses- Continuous consumption of contaminated food can
  • result in chronic illnesses such as hormonal imbalance, reproductive problems, and
  • developmental disorders.
  • • Loss of Consumer Trust- Damages consumer confidence in domestic and export food
  • markets.

  • Each questions carries (10 marks)

questions.question: Define food hygiene and explain its importance in ensuring food safety.
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: Food Hygiene refers to the conditions and practices necessary to ensure the safety
  • cleanliness, and wholesomeness of food at all stages—from production and processing
  • to preparation and consumption. This includes proper handling, preparation, storage
  • and distribution of food to prevent contamination and foodborne illnesses.
  • • Prevention of Foodborne Diseases- Good food hygiene practices help eliminate
  • harmful bacteria, viruses, and parasites that can cause serious health problems like
  • food poisoning, diarrhoea, and infections.
  • • Promotion of public health- Proper food hygiene practices reduce spread of
  • infectious disease, especially in communities and food establishments.
  • • Enhanced Food quality and safety – Sanitation ensures that food is free from
  • contaminants maintaining its nutritional value, flavor and quality.
  • • Compliance with regulations- Adhering to food safety laws and standards, avoid legal
  • consequences, penalties and laws of reputations, consumer trust.
  • • Economic benefits – Reduces healthcare host and loss productivity.
  • • Protection of vulnerable – Children, pregnant women elderly and those with the
  • weakened immune systems are particularly risk from food borne illness, making
  • hygienic conditions is essential for those populations.
  • • Environmental impact- Proper waste management in food production and
  • preparation minimizes environmental pollution, contributing to sustainability.
questions.final_answer: preparation minimizes environmental pollution, contributing to sustainability

questions.question: Write a detailed note on how relative humidity and water activity affects / the growth of microrganisms.
questions.solution_html:
• of microorganism?
  • Ans: The growth and survival of microorganisms in food are heavily influenced by moisture
  • related factors, primarily relative humidity (RH) and water activity (aw).
  • Relative Humidity- Relative Humidity is the amount of moisture present in the air compared
  • to the maximum it can hold at a given temperature, expressed as a percentage.
  • • Impact on Food- RH affects the moisture content of foods during storage. If the RH is
  • too high, dry foods may absorb moisture, tends to microbial growth.
  • • Microbial Growth- Molds and some bacteria can grow on food surfaces when RH is
  • high.
  • • Control Measures- Proper packaging and environmental control help maintain
  • optimal RH and minimize microbial risks.
  • Water Activity- Water activity is a measure of the free or available water in a food product
  • for microbial use.
  • • Different microorganisms have minimum aw requirements for growth.
  • • Lowering aw through drying, freezing, or adding solutes like salt and sugar is a
  • common method to preserve food and prevent microbial spoilage
questions.final_answer: common method to preserve food and prevent microbial spoilage

questions.question: What are the preventive measures to control food borne pathogens?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: Foodborne pathogens such as Salmonella, E. coli, Listeria, and Norovirus are
  • responsible for millions of food-related illnesses globally. Preventing contamination and
  • controlling these pathogens is essential for ensuring food safety.
  • • Personal Hygiene- Regular handwashing with soap and clean water, especially after
  • using the toilet or handling raw food. Use of clean uniforms, gloves, and hairnets to
  • prevent contamination.
  • • Proper Cooking and Temperature Control- Cook food to the correct internal
  • temperature to kill pathogens.
  • • Safe Storage and Refrigeration- Store perishable items in the refrigerator or freezer.
  • Avoid leaving cooked or perishable food at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
  • • Cross-Contamination Prevention- Use separate cutting boards, utensils, and
  • containers for raw and cooked foods.
  • • Cleaning and Sanitization- Regularly clean and sanitize kitchen surfaces, equipment
  • and utensils.
  • • Waste management- Proper disposal of food waste to avoid attracting pests or
  • causing contamination.
  • • Pest Control- Keep food storage and preparation areas clean and sealed. Implement
  • pest control programs.

questions.question: Define food hygiene and explain its importance in ensuring food safety.
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: Food Hygiene refers to the conditions and practices necessary to ensure the safety
  • cleanliness, and wholesomeness of food at all stages—from production and processing
  • to preparation and consumption. This includes proper handling, preparation, storage
  • and distribution of food to prevent contamination and foodborne illnesses.
  • • Prevention of Foodborne Diseases- Good food hygiene practices help eliminate
  • harmful bacteria, viruses, and parasites that can cause serious health problems like
  • food poisoning, diarrhoea, and infections.
  • • Promotion of public health- Proper food hygiene practices reduce spread of
  • infectious disease, especially in communities and food establishments.
  • • Enhanced Food quality and safety – Sanitation ensures that food is free from
  • contaminants maintaining its nutritional value, flavor and quality.
  • • Compliance with regulations- Adhering to food safety laws and standards, avoid legal
  • consequences, penalties and laws of reputations, consumer trust.
  • • Economic benefits – Reduces healthcare host and loss productivity.
  • • Protection of vulnerable – Children, pregnant women elderly and those with the
  • weakened immune systems are particularly risk from food borne illness, making
  • hygienic conditions is essential for those populations.
  • • Environmental impact- Proper waste management in food production and
  • preparation minimizes environmental pollution, contributing to sustainability.
questions.final_answer: preparation minimizes environmental pollution, contributing to sustainability

questions.question: Write a detailed note on how relative humidity and water activity affects / the growth of microrganisms.
questions.solution_html:
• of microorganism?
  • Ans: The growth and survival of microorganisms in food are heavily influenced by moisture
  • related factors, primarily relative humidity (RH) and water activity (aw).
  • Relative Humidity- Relative Humidity is the amount of moisture present in the air compared
  • to the maximum it can hold at a given temperature, expressed as a percentage.
  • • Impact on Food- RH affects the moisture content of foods during storage. If the RH is
  • too high, dry foods may absorb moisture, tends to microbial growth.
  • • Microbial Growth- Molds and some bacteria can grow on food surfaces when RH is
  • high.
  • • Control Measures- Proper packaging and environmental control help maintain
  • optimal RH and minimize microbial risks.
  • Water Activity- Water activity is a measure of the free or available water in a food product
  • for microbial use.
  • • Different microorganisms have minimum aw requirements for growth.
  • • Lowering aw through drying, freezing, or adding solutes like salt and sugar is a
  • common method to preserve food and prevent microbial spoilage
questions.final_answer: common method to preserve food and prevent microbial spoilage

questions.question: What are the preventive measures to control food borne pathogens?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: Foodborne pathogens such as Salmonella, E. coli, Listeria, and Norovirus are
  • responsible for millions of food-related illnesses globally. Preventing contamination and
  • controlling these pathogens is essential for ensuring food safety.
  • • Personal Hygiene- Regular handwashing with soap and clean water, especially after
  • using the toilet or handling raw food. Use of clean uniforms, gloves, and hairnets to
  • prevent contamination.
  • • Proper Cooking and Temperature Control- Cook food to the correct internal
  • temperature to kill pathogens.
  • • Safe Storage and Refrigeration- Store perishable items in the refrigerator or freezer.
  • Avoid leaving cooked or perishable food at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
  • • Cross-Contamination Prevention- Use separate cutting boards, utensils, and
  • containers for raw and cooked foods.
  • • Cleaning and Sanitization- Regularly clean and sanitize kitchen surfaces, equipment
  • and utensils.
  • • Waste management- Proper disposal of food waste to avoid attracting pests or
  • causing contamination.
  • • Pest Control- Keep food storage and preparation areas clean and sealed. Implement
  • pest control programs.
